claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr can remain a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy in a high-temperature equilibrium state containing percolated SRO clusters before phase separation.
Percolation of SRO clusters causes a nonlinear, abrupt reduction in lattice thermal conductivity.
The conductivity reduction caused by SRO percolation exceeds predictions from serial/parallel mixing models and point-defect scattering theories.
A percolating SRO network introduces a dominant scattering channel for mid-to-high-frequency phonons.
The percolating SRO network creates a phonon-glass-like transport regime within the BCC crystal.
Changing the interatomic potential energy surface can control SRO strength, correlation length, and the transition from isolated clusters to a percolating network.
Moment Tensor Potentials trained on DFT data can capture preferences for particular local pairs and drive SRO percolation at selected temperatures in HfNbTaTiZr.
SRO is thermodynamically stable but not fully ordered in single-phase BCC HfNbTaTiZr between 800 K and 1500 K.
TDTR or laser flash analysis can isolate the lattice contribution to thermal conductivity in this alloy.
Percolating SRO clusters act as extended phonon-scattering centers distinct from isolated point defects.
Phonon transport in BCC refractory HEAs is dominated by lattice vibrations.
SRO percolation produces a spatially correlated modulation of atomic masses and force constants.
The correlated SRO network preferentially scatters phonons whose wavelengths are comparable to the cluster size and spacing.

Percolation creates a topological change in the phonon mean-free-path distribution, producing a sharper conductivity decrease than the linear concentration dependence expected from simple defect scattering.
Vibrational-disorder effects reported for high-entropy carbide systems provide an analogy for phonon-glass-like transport in BCC refractory HEAs.
SRO percolation is expected when the cluster volume fraction exceeds approximately 0.3 to 0.4.
After percolation, lattice thermal conductivity will fall an additional 20% to 40% relative to the reduction expected from random mixing.
Thermal conductivity depends more strongly on SRO-network topology than on global composition.
The proposed control is a random solid solution of identical composition with uncorrelated point-defect scattering and no SRO contribution.
A linear conductivity decrease without a threshold, or agreement with the random-solid-solution prediction despite an observed percolating SRO network, would falsify the percolation mechanism.

contradictions.description: The initial state is defined as already containing a percolated SRO network, whereas the intervention and experiment require a sequence spanning random, isolated-cluster, and percolated states. The reference state of the hypothesis is therefore inconsistent or at least ambiguously defined.
